source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The bone marrow is suppressing erythropoiesis despite the recent blood loss.","B":"The bone marrow is increasing red blood cell production to replace cells lost through hemorrhage.","C":"The finding reflects increased platelet production rather than a red-cell marrow response.","D":"The result indicates iron overload caused by the recent hemorrhage."}}
source_row.rationale: Reticulocytes are immature red blood cells released from bone marrow. A higher reticulocyte count can occur after new or ongoing bleeding because the marrow increases red blood cell production to replace lost cells.
source_row.source_detail: Higher reticulocyte count after bleeding reflects increased replacement red blood cell production Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client recovering from substantial blood loss has a higher-than-normal reticulocyte count. What does this finding most likely indicate?
